children: , the integrated oil-and-gas producer, caught a powerful commodity boost Thursday as Brent crude surged 4% to $105.26 per barrel. The stock initially rallied roughly 2.1% to $167.67 before surrendering nearly the entire advance and trading at $164.01. That sharp reversal shows investors are treating the oil spike as both an earnings tailwind and an economic warning.

The company produced $14.5 billion in second-quarter earnings and $17.2 billion in free cash flow. Upstream operations contributed $7.93 billion, representing approximately 54.6% of total earnings. One quarter's free cash flow alone equals about 2.3% of Exxon's $738 billion market capitalization, giving the company serious financial firepower if crude remains elevated.

Yet the valuation picture demands discipline. The image places Exxon's $164.01 share price 28.79% above its GF Value of $127.35, signaling that plenty of optimism may already be priced in. Annualizing the latest quarter implies a free-cash-flow yield above 9%, but conflict-driven oil profits are unreliable: expensive crude can lift upstream earnings while damaging consumption, inflation and economic growth. Exxon's fading rally captures the trade perfectly$105 oil is great for today's cash flow, but potentially dangerous for tomorrow's demand.

title: Exxon Rally Fades as Brent Crude Jumps 4% Above $105
